industry.why: Neutral, carried, balanced on new evidence both ways. Component 1 regime, 23-Oct-26 (risk-off confirmed and broadening: the discount-rate squeeze now a positioning wash-out in the artificial intelligence complex with credit leading it, bonds rallied as a hedge for the first time this cycle while the Fed still hikes in December, the US 10-year near 5.10%, Brent $111, French sovereign stress spilling into Italy, European defensives leading cyclicals on all five windows and breadth in the bottom fifth of three years; sources present 2026-W43): two houses call a cyclical upturn, DNB Carnegie (22 Oct) reading Sandvik and Metso as a new mining cycle and Danske (18 Oct) heavy trucks and pulp and paper turning, and Goldman's economists (16 Oct) have US industrial production beating with machinery and electrical equipment near peak capacity use; against it, Danske's own warning that most cyclical exposure is 'more or less at all-time highs' with 'cost inflation emerging', a risk-off regime confirmed on all five defensive windows, and Relative strength per 31-relative-strength.md, 2026-10-23 against 2026-08-21, not week on week: D now, C prior at industry level. The sector rows do the work: Electrical equipment and grid, Diversified groups, Distributors and Test and measurement at C, Flow control and Building technology at D. Counter-case for B: the order data are the strongest non-AI demand read in the pack; for D: the tape and the regime.

sector.why: Neutral, set deliberately this week (carried C). Component 1 regime, 16-Oct-26 (a discount-rate shock with the first credit crack inside the artificial intelligence chain: United States core inflation re-accelerating on energy, the Fed and Bank of England hikes pulled forward, the US 10-year about 5.1%, the US joined the sell-off and Asia is in washout, defensives bid for four weeks in Europe, European breadth off its three-year lows but in the bottom quarter, the consumer forecast to weaken into winter; sources present 2026-W42): diversified industrial groups are cyclical capital goods into a growth scare, but their diversification is itself the simple, proven profile the regime pays for, and Relative strength per 31-relative-strength.md, 2026-10-16 against 2026-08-14, not week on week: A now, C prior, says the market is paying for it. Three memos this week in this Sector all turn on the Fragility axis, not on the Sector: Beijer Alma (Mixed) and Idun Industrier (Fights it) are small, geared, re-rating-dependent Swedish acquirers, thyssenkrupp (Mixed) is large but 'neither simple nor proven'; the Fragility row carries that judgement, so the Sector row does not double it. One live holding, Sdiptech (5.05%, Sell-side and Thematic Fit A). Counter-case for higher: leadership and six MI Pool names with Thematic Fit B; for lower: the group's small acquirers are what a credit crack hurts first. Neutral by judgement.

memo.verdict: Neutral; park at this price; conviction medium, a working hypothesis at Triaging. Aalberts is a cyclical recovery with a self-help overlay, priced as if the recovery were already normal: at 41.96 EUR (2026-09-23) the modal path pays about 14 percent a year over eighteen months and about 12 percent over three years, short of the 20 percent bar, and clears the bar only on a re-rating to about 14.3x the record calls possible (about 30 percent), not probable. The park rule does not park it (management C, business quality C, predictability C, trackability B); the return does. Progress triggers named: the price at or below about 39 EUR, where the modal path clears 20 percent a year over eighteen months (about 40 EUR at the blended multiple); German and French residential permits rising for two quarters, which would raise the modal path itself and make the thesis a B without a re-rating; or the sell-side earnings-momentum pin catching up with FactSet's series, which removes the stale F without changing the return. Invalidation triggers: two consecutive quarters of Semicon organic decline; added-value margin below 60 percent for two periods.
case: The thesis: a cyclical recovery with a self-help overlay, priced as if the recovery were already normal; at 41.96 EUR the shares pay about 14 percent a year over eighteen months and 12 percent over three on the modal path, and the case clears the 20 percent bar only on a re-rating called possible, not probable.

The external change is a sector-wide semiconductor-equipment upcycle in the reported numbers: Semicon organic +16.4 percent in 2Q26 against consensus 3.3 percent; segment EBITA +88 percent to 47.5 EURm on 335.7 EURm revenue in 1H26; ASML backlog 38.8 billion EUR; ASML EUV capacity plan 110 systems by 2028; Huatai memory capex compounding 36 percent a year to 2028. It acts on 15 percent of FY2025 revenue, a strong force and not a group-wide one. The internal change is broad and executed: seven of twelve screen forces active, three strong (perimeter A, acquisitions B, standards B); about 400 EURm of low-margin revenue removed in five months, worth over 100 basis points of FY2026 margin; Paulo and Grand Venture Technology bought in higher-margin niches; a 50 EURm restructuring for 25 EURm of savings; a whole-team change inside eighteen months (finance director April 2025, operations director October 2024, chief strategy officer, chief marketing and digital officer, two divisional chief executives, three supervisory board members); a 75 EURm buyback a year. Both forces act in the same direction: capital is going where the external force is strongest and leaving where the headwind sits.

The chain breaks at the largest segment: Building is 50 percent of revenue, its European residential markets are at a trough management calls severe, Building EBITA fell 3 percent to 100.4 EURm and missed 104.0 EURm consensus, France, the United Kingdom and Eastern Europe are "highly challenging" with Benelux, the Nordics and Germany "gradually improving"; the modal path builds in no European turn (possible, about 40 percent).
counter_case: Two counter-cases the record carried at full force, one on the fundamentals and one on the price.

Against the fundamentals, the "false friend" of the risks report of 8 June 2026: the first-half beat is a cyclical bounce dressed as a structural turn. About half of the 90 basis point margin gain is the arithmetic of deconsolidating KAN and Metalis (50 to 60 basis points on Bernstein's count, 70 to 80 on the risks report's), not operating improvement. Building EBITA fell 3 percent to 100.4 EURm and missed 104.0 EURm consensus. Holding costs rose to 13.6 EURm in the half, 3.6 EURm above consensus, and Jefferies raised modelled holding costs to 27 EURm, which is why its FY2026 EBITA did not move on a revenue upgrade. European residential building in Germany, France and the United Kingdom is still in a severe cyclical trough. FY2025 cash conversion of 64 percent was flattered by a 155 EURm inventory release; FactSet's free cash flow was 47.7 EURm, 32 percent of reported net income, and did not cover the 124 EURm of dividends paid on that definition. Metalis was sold at about 5x EV/EBITA the same year Grand Venture Technology was bought at 10.5x EV/EBITDA, an "unusual valuation arbitrage" shareholders criticised. Restructuring has been charged at 40 to 55 EURm every year since 2020 with benefits "frequently omitted", so "structural" savings have a way of being re-spent. A chief executive whose stated style is "under-promise, over-deliver" over-promised for two years (FY2024 organic -3.4 percent against 4 to 6 percent guided; FY2025 -2.5 percent against flat; margin from 15.0 to 13.2 percent against 16 to 18 percent targeted) and after one good half guides only qualitatively while the sell-side and the price extrapolate. Both covering brokers disbelieve the 18 percent 2030 target (16.3 and 17.0 percent). Former division executives describe a loose federation with no central purchasing, competing sister companies and transfer-pricing distortions, whose margin target needs a European volume recovery that may never come, and whose Semicon moat is a single customer's design cycle; ASML's frame contracts run over years, so an 86 percent jump in ASML's order intake does not translate one-for-one; the segment fell 17.8 percent organic in 3Q25 and can turn fast in both directions. The risks report's analysis argues the failure modes are correlated through the European cycle, so "the collective probability of zero failures during the hold period is low". No insider bought below 25 EUR in late 2025. The record concedes all of this on the price and most of it on the mix of the margin gain; it holds the fundamentals because the Semicon acceleration is reported (revenue 335.7 EURm, EBITA +88 percent to 47.5 EURm), corroborated by ASML's backlog, the 110-system EUV plan and Dronten commissioning in early 2027; the Industry margin of 18.6 percent (20.1 percent in 2Q26) is a record and not a deconsolidation effect; and the 63.0 percent added-value margin held through the downturn is proven. Where the competing hypothesis wins is on the price, and that is where the rating sits.
triggers: - Progress: price at or below about 39 EUR (modal path clears 20 percent a year over eighteen months; about 40 EUR at the blended multiple; below 34.5 EUR over three years).

- Progress: German and French residential permits rising for two quarters (raises the modal path; thesis a B without re-rating). Alarm: permits down three quarters running; a 20 percent jump is the disconfirmation of the Building risk.
- Progress: the earnings-momentum pin catching up with FactSet's series (removes the stale F; return unchanged).
- Invalidate: two consecutive quarters of Semicon organic decline; added-value margin below 60 percent for two periods.

- Alarm: ASML guiding to the 4 percent low end of its range; Grand Venture Technology organic growth below 10 percent; second half of 2026 below 14.4 percent EBITA margin; holding costs above 30 EURm for the year; Thrive 2030 timeline pushed beyond two years; leverage above 2.3x without a named acquisition; a year without a buyback.
- Semicon ramp: does Semicon EBITA reach a quarter or more of the group by the FY2027 results (probable, about 60 percent)?
